correctness.rationale: For nonzero finite-rank H_{bar psi} with psi∈BMOA_0, compactness and weak nullness of normalized Hardy kernels at |a|→1 imply any SRKT norm equality is attained at some interior k_a. Classical Kronecker finite rank forces rational psi analytic with no closed-disk poles and hence bounded; the normalized disk involution phi_a transports k_a to the origin. Set g=psi∘phi_a-psi(a). Nehari distance dist(bar psi,H∞) is invariant under boundary composition phi_a and constants; the Poisson harmonic-measure/Bonsall kernel variance gives ||g||_2²=P(|psi|²)(a)-|psi(a)|²=||H_{bar psi}k_a||². Thus the transformed g has minimal Hankel norm equal to ||g||_2. Brevig–Seip Theorem 1, inspected in the original primary PDF, states minimal implies maximal norm, and simultaneous L² and L∞ equality forces constant boundary modulus; rational inner g=C I must be a finite Blaschke. Undo phi_a and g(0)=0 yields psi=C(B-B(0)). Conversely Bonsall for finite B gives ||H_{bar psi}k_a||²=|C|²(1-|B(a)|²), norm |C| and zeros exactly norming kernels; ker H_{bar B}=BH² gives rank deg(B), while sup_boundary|B-B(0)|=1+|B(0)|. The phase factor on H_{bar psi}=conj(C)H_{bar B}, not C, is an immaterial typographical scalar issue in the package proof: ranks and norms are unchanged. Analytic rationality, finite Blaschke and boundary arguments establish all degrees; finite matrix spot checks are not a proof.
